Hi Lena —

Thanks again for taking time on today's discovery call. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep the contracting track moving: 

1) DPA preference: You mentioned legal prefers a short-form DPA with SCC modules added. To proceed we need confirmation whether Paybridge intends to be the data controller for customer data flows (as we discussed) or whether there are any joint-controller considerations for the product integration. That decision will determine the DPA variant we propose.

2) SCC module selection: Redwood supports the standard EU SCCs plus the module-based approach for processor-to-processor relationships. If Paybridge prefers module-based tailoring (modules II/III), we’ll flag the required security appendices.

3) SOC 2 / security questionnaire: Please share the vendor security questionnaire you referenced (we can take first pass answers). I’m attaching a short DPA options summary and can also return a prefilled questionnaire to speed review.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Options_Summary.pdf (summary of short-form vs full DPA + SCC module impact).

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm controller role (Paybridge controller vs joint controller) by EOD Wed 5/5.
- Share the security questionnaire (or a link) so Marcus can start filling technical controls.
- If helpful, we can set a 30-min legal-to-legal call with your counsel and Laura (Redwood legal) next week.

I’m looping Marcus on technical/QoS questions and Laura for contract/legal.

Best,
Naomi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Naomi / team — quick recommendation for the Paybridge thread: 

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Redwood is the processor. We should state this clearly in our response to avoid joint-controller ambiguity.

2) SCC module: For their described use (Paybridge retains customer transaction data; Redwood receives inference payloads and returns derived responses), the standard Processor-to-Processor path (Module I/II) is appropriate. Recommend we propose the SCC 'Processor-to-Processor' clause (module II) + processor appendices covering technical measures. This keeps obligations clear and limits third-party liability.

3) DPA variant: Offer the short-form DPA with an appendix referencing our SOC 2 Type II report (latest period) and a SOC 2 addendum link rather than embedding full attestation text. That balances speed with evidence. Laura — please confirm the language (I drafted a 2-line clause below).

Draft clause (suggested): 
"Redwood is the processor of customer personal data for the purposes set out in the Agreement. Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering security controls relevant to processing; Redwood will provide Paybridge a current SOC 2 summary and allow for reasonable evidence review under NDA."

4) Timeline: If Paybridge confirms controller role today (5/5) we can return a prefilled questionnaire and DPA short-form + SCC selection by EOD 5/6. Marcus — flag any questionnaire items that need engineering input; I’ll coordinate with Laura for legal phrasing.

Happy to jump on the legal-2-legal Friday slot if scheduled.

— Karthik
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
